chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Uthman, from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali, who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) delivered a sermon, in which he praised God and extolled Him, then sent blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), then said:

Beware! Indeed, the two things I fear most for you are: following vain desires and prolonged hope. As for following vain desires, it diverts from the truth; and as for prolonged hope, it causes the Hereafter to be forgotten.

Beware! The world has set out departing, and the Hereafter has set out approaching. Each of them has children, so be of the children of the Hereafter and do not be of the children of the world. For today is the day of deeds and no reckoning, while tomorrow is the day of reckoning and no deeds. The origin of tribulations is the following of desires and the introduction of invented rulings by which God's command is opposed, wherein men take authority over men.

Beware! Indeed, if truth were pure (unmixed), there would be no disagreement; and if falsehood were pure, it would not be hidden from one who has intellect. But a handful is taken from this (truth) and a handful from this (falsehood), and the two are mixed together and covered up, and therein Satan gains control over his allies, while those for whom God's grace was predestined are saved.

Indeed I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) say: 'How will you be when a tribulation envelops you, in which the young grows up and the old grows old, the people run upon it and take it as their Sunnah, so when something of it is changed it is said: the Sunnah has been changed and the people have committed an abomination! Then the calamity intensifies, the offspring are taken captive, and the tribulation crushes them as fire crushes firewood and as a millstone grinds with its lower stone — and they seek religious knowledge for other than God, and they learn for other than practice, and they seek the world through the deeds of the Hereafter.'

Then he turned his face while around him were people from his household, close companions, and followers, and said: 'The rulers before me performed actions in which they deliberately opposed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), violated his covenant, and changed his Sunnah. If I had compelled the people to abandon these (innovations) and restored them to their proper places and to what they were during the time of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), my army would have dispersed from me until I was left alone or with few of my followers who knew my virtue and the obligation of my imamate from the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, and the Sunnah of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family).'

Consider: if I commanded the Station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to be returned to the place where the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had placed it, and returned Fadak to the heirs of Fatima (peace be upon her), and returned the sa' of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) as it was, and carried out the land grants that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had granted to certain peoples but which had not been executed or implemented for them —

And returned the house of Jafar to his heirs and demolished it from the mosque; and returned the judgments of injustice that had been passed, and separated women who were unjustly held by men, returning them to their husbands, and applied to them the ruling concerning marital matters and laws; and captured the offspring of Banu Taghlib, and returned what was divided of the land of Khaybar; and abolished the registers of stipends and distributed as the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to give — equally — and had not made it a resource circulating among the wealthy; and removed the land measurement, and equalized among marriages, and implemented the khums of the Messenger as God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed and made obligatory —

And returned the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) to what it was, closing what doors had been opened in it, and opening what had been closed; and prohibited wiping over leather socks, and applied the hadd punishment for nabidh, and commanded the permissibility of the two mut'as; and commanded the five takbirs over funeral prayers, and obligated the people to recite the Bismillah aloud; and expelled those who had been admitted to his mosque who the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had expelled, and admitted those who had been expelled after the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) whom he had admitted —

And I compelled the people to follow the ruling of the Quran and divorce according to the Sunnah, and collected the zakah according to its categories and limits; and returned the ritual ablution (wudu), the major ablution (ghusl), and the prayer to their proper times, prescribed laws, and places; and returned the people of Najran to their homes, and returned the captives of Persia and other peoples to the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) —

In that case they would have dispersed from me! By God, I commanded the people not to gather during the month of Ramadan except for the obligatory (prayers), and I informed them that their gathering for supererogatory prayers is an innovation (bid'a). Then some of the people of my army who were fighting with me cried out: 'O people of Islam, the Sunnah of Umar has been changed! He forbids us from praying in the month of Ramadan voluntarily!' And indeed I feared they would revolt in a corner of my camp.

What I have suffered from this community — from division and obedience to imams of misguidance and callers to the Fire! And I gave from that the share of those with close kinship (dhul-qurba), about which God, Mighty and Majestic, said:
«If you have believed in God and in what We revealed to Our servant on the Day of the Criterion, the Day when the two armies met» (Quran 8:41)
By God, it is we whom He meant by dhul-qurba (those with close kinship), He who coupled us with Himself and with His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). And He, the Exalted, said:

«So for God, for the Messenger, and for those with close kinship, the orphans, the poor, and the wayfarer» — specifically about us — «so that it does not become rotating wealth among the wealthy among you. What the Messenger brought you, take it; and what he forbade you from, abstain from it. And fear God regarding wronging the family of Muhammad. Indeed, God is severe in punishment for those who wrong them» — as a mercy from Him for us and wealth/sufficiency with which God has made us self-sufficient.

And He enjoined it upon His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and He did not assign for us from the share of sadaqah any portion. God honored His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) and honored us, the People of the House, by not feeding us from the filth of the people.

So they denied God and denied His Messenger, and repudiated the Book of God that speaks clearly of our rights, and withheld from us an obligation that God made obligatory for us. No household of a prophet has suffered from his community what we have suffered after our Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). And God is the one from whom help is sought against those who wronged us, and there is no power or strength except with God, the Most High, the Greatest.

key_terms.الْبِدْعَةُ: Bid'ah — innovation in religion; practice introduced without prophetic basis
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: Khums — the one-fifth religious tax mandated in Quran 8:41 for Ahl al-Bayt and specified categories
key_terms.الْفِتْنَةُ: Tribulation, strife, sedition — a period of religious confusion and social disorder
key_terms.الْهَوَى: Vain desire, passion, caprice — the internal impulse that leads one away from truth and virtue
key_terms.ذُو الْقُرْبَى: Kin relatives/near of kin — in Shia interpretation, refers specifically to the Ahlulbayt
key_terms.طُولُ الْأَمَلِ: Prolonged hope — excessive attachment to worldly life that causes heedlessness of the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about vain desires, prolonged hope, and the rights of Ahlulbayt in his sermon?
ai.summary: This is one of the most significant political and jurisprudential sermons of Imam Ali (AS), delivered during his caliphate to a general audience and then privately to his household and Shia. Imam Ali warns of two spiritual dangers — following vain desires and prolonged worldly hope — before quoting the Prophet's prophecy about a tribulation-ridden era. He then addresses his close followers, cataloguing the numerous religious and legal innovations introduced by his predecessors that he would have reversed had he not feared losing all political support. The sermon climaxes in a defense of the Ahlulbayt's right to khums from Quran 8:41 and 59:7, and ends with a lament over the oppression inflicted on the Prophet's family.
